rationale: Answers the parent investigation's registered gap (838461385f784f74af057837ff488a66-gap-3: does anything inside the sealed configuration bound or repair the reported index drift after many more re-synchronization rounds and further leader changes?) with a concrete successor experiment. The harness gains one case, stopsign_drift_bound_probe, which keeps the lineage prefix (node 3 leads, five entries decided, StopSign decided, six indices of content) and then (a) performs eight further rounds of node1.reconnected(3)+node2.reconnected(3), (b) elects node 1, one of the two inflated followers, as the new leader with try_become_leader() and samples all three nodes, and (c) performs three more rounds in which the remaining replicas re-synchronize with that new leader. Every round samples each node separately under a distinct event name (BOUND_R{k}_N{pid}); each round's queue drain and its samples run together under one catch_unwind, as does the leader change, so a panic raised inside a message handler or inside a storage read is reported as BOUND_STAGES.panics instead of aborting the run. The decided-log endpoint (read_decided_suffix(0)) is sampled in every round, so the unreadability of the decided log is measured across all rounds rather than at one point. No records other than this experiment are changed: the drift account and its four witnessed consequence classes stand, the two child accounts are untouched, and no conclusion is drawn before the receipt exists. Still open and untouched this turn: the trim child's storage-route gap (b26c13954e184cd2b9fdfda975aff136-gap-4) and the snapshot discriminator's equal-index/follower-side/peer-side variants.

scope.description: Nine cases in one execution over three real OmniPaxos instances in one process with MemoryStorage and a deterministic FIFO in-process network; the new case keeps the lineage prefix and then re-synchronizes the two followers eight further times, replaces the leader with one of those inflated followers, and re-synchronizes the remaining replicas three more times against the new leader, sampling all three nodes every round and reporting any handler panic as an event field rather than aborting the run.
assumptions: Entry type Value has Snapshot = NoSnapshot; ClusterConfig { configuration_id: 1, nodes: [1,2,3], flexible_quorum: None } with default ServerConfig (batch_size 1); BLE messages are dropped, as in the lineage.

A round is node1.reconnected(3) plus node2.reconnected(3) followed by a drain of the queue; after the leader change the followers report the new leader, i.e. node2.reconnected(1) plus node3.reconnected(1), because reconnected(pid) only triggers a re-synchronization when pid is the current leader.

AcceptSync/Promise traffic is generated by the library itself; the harness only supplies the re-established connections and drains the queue, so the resume points are the library's own reported accepted indexes.

catch_unwind wraps each round's drain together with that round's samples, and separately the leader change, so a panic inside a handler or inside a storage read becomes the BOUND_STAGES.panics count; it does not change protocol behaviour when no panic occurs.
excluded: No entry type with use_snapshots() true is used in the new case, and no compaction is requested in it, so trim and snapshot over-compaction are out of this case's scope.
No node restart, storage loss, timers or message loss are exercised; only the reconnected() path and the ordinary leader-change path.
No crate or package test suite is executed; only the generated test file.

experiment.prefix: Same prefix as the lineage: node 3 leads, five entries are appended and decided, then a StopSign is proposed with reconfigure() and decided, so every node holds six indices of content and reports accepted 6 / decided 6 (BOUND_BASE). The new case then performs eight rounds of node1.reconnected(3)+node2.reconnected(3); each round drains the queue and samples node 1, node 2 and node 3 separately as BOUND_R{k}_N1, BOUND_R{k}_N2 and BOUND_R{k}_N3 for k = 1..8, all inside one catch_unwind. It then calls node1.try_become_leader() inside catch_unwind, drains, and samples all three nodes as BOUND_AFTER_LEADER_CHANGE. Finally it performs three rounds of node2.reconnected(1)+node3.reconnected(1), each drained and sampled as BOUND_R9..R11, and emits BOUND_STAGES with the number of rounds and the number of guarded stages that panicked, followed by BOUND_RUN_END. Every sample records accepted_idx, decided_idx, decided_eq_accepted, is_reconfigured, the read of index 5, the read of index 6, the read of the decided suffix from 0 and its length.
semantic_changes: Adds the drift-bound case stopsign_drift_bound_probe together with the drive_round and sample_guarded helpers; every previously generated case is unchanged apart from sharing one execution.

comparisons.description: Eight further re-synchronization rounds do not push the first follower's reported accepted index past the six indices of content it holds.
Eight further re-synchronization rounds do not push the second follower's reported accepted index past the six indices of content it holds.
While the followers keep re-synchronizing, the leader's decided index stays within the entries the leader itself holds.
The leader's decided log remains readable from index 0 after eight further re-synchronization rounds.
A new leader adopts a log it actually holds: after node 1 takes the lead its reported accepted index equals its six indices of content rather than a drifted report.
Three rounds after the leader change the drift has not been repaired: the follower's reported accepted index is still within the six indices of content it holds.
Three rounds after the leader change the third replica's decided index is still covered by the entries it holds.
No guarded round, sample or leader change panics while the drift continues over eleven rounds.

experiment.revision_reason: Adds the drift-bound case stopsign_drift_bound_probe: eight further re-synchronization rounds, a leader change onto one of the inflated followers, and three further rounds against that new leader, with every round sampled per node and every queue drain panic-guarded. The harness also carries the drift-then-trim and drift-then-snapshot cases added by the child investigations, which are unchanged.
